LESSON: TAKING AWAY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Numbers
Topic 2.8: Taking Away
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Taking Away, part of Numbers in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: How many objects are in each group? 2. How many objects are left after taking away some objects?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Collect in purposive pairs/group different groups of similar concrete objects from the school environment as they observe safety. Learners with manipulative difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or be assisted by peers, learner support assistants or the teacher to collect objects. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Collect in purposive pairs/group different groups of similar concrete objects from the school environment as they observe safety. Learners with manipulative difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or be assisted by peers, learner support assistants or the teacher to collect objects. B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Taking Away together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and problem solving: learners take away not more than 9 objects from groups of similar objects and count the

remainder.

Values:
Respect: learners exercise patience and take turns as they carry out take away activities with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety: learners carefully collect concrete objects to use in taking away activities.

Link to Other Activity Areas:

The learner is able to relate collecting of different groups of similar objects from the environment to keeping the environment

clean in Environmental Activities.
